newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Flexible EMU entry seen agreed at Ecofin-Sweden.
newsitem.headline: Flexible EMU entry seen agreed at Ecofin-Sweden.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Friday that EU Finance Ministers will probably agree this weekend that countries should be allowed to move from the planned exchange rate mechanism ERM2 to Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) at different times.

"You can theoretically imagine that the issue (EMU membership) will be on the agenda at different points in time for different countries," Asbrink told journalists after a meeting with the Swedish parliament's EU committee.
"There should be flexibility so you don't have to stand in the waiting room for a long time to wait for other countries."
The issue will be discussed at this weekend's informal Ecofin meeting in the Dutch town of Noordwijk.
"I should think this line of policy will be the result," Asbrink said. "At the same time the voluntary nature of ERM2 is important, an issue Sweden has brought up," he added.
ERM2 is planned to replace the current exchange rate mechanism (ERM) when EMU starts on January 1, 1999. ERM2 will encompass EU currencies not participating in EMU.
